name: The Glassgrass Basin
region_detail: An exposed depression in the open eastern grasslands.
site_type: basin | Natural wonders | Seasonal salt pan and unusual mineralized grassland.
history: Seasonal floods collect in this shallow depression and evaporate during the warmer months, leaving a crust of pale mineral salts. Grass growing around the basin accumulates translucent deposits along its blades, which catch the sunlight and produce a glasslike sheen. Varkesh and Rathen travelers have long recognized the site as a useful landmark.
current_state: The basin remains a customary stop for migrating animals and herders seeking salt. During dry weather, the firm outer crust supports foot traffic, though soft mud may persist beneath its center. No permanent settlement or commercial claim has been established.
inhabitants: Wild grazing animals, small birds, occasional herding parties, and travelers.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; localized hazards include concealed soft mud and the lack of potable water.
points_of_interest:
Mineralized grass; seasonal salt pan; animal trails; isolated boulders used as landmarks; a shallow rainwater pool along the upper rim; sheltered resting ground outside the basin.

Unresolved elements: Whether the mineral deposits possess any unusual practical properties.; How far seasonal flooding extends.; Whether future travelers, merchants, or settlers develop an interest in the site.
discovery: An exposed depression in the open eastern grasslands. Travelers may notice the reflection of sunlight from the basin or follow animal trails toward it. Herders familiar with the surrounding plains know the site.
